Another reason why I think aggro/zoo-ish decks dominates this brawl is because low drops have a much larger increase in value due to the bananas. By being the aggressor, you're more likely to have minions on the board, which means you get more options to trade while using the banana buffs to ensure you get the upper hand on these trades.

Additionally, low cost cards have their value proportionately increased much more than higher drops. For example, going from wisp to "wisp, deathrattle: add a banana to your hand" is a much larger bump in value than, say, going from Ysera to "Ysera, deathrattle: add a banana to your hand"

I feel like its not the "death rattle" that is where the value is at but the buffing of the minion themselves. A wisp for 0 mana is okay but a 2 2 for 1 mana is a larger value gain than a ysera becoming a 10 mana 5 13.
Limitless Power comes through a steady diet of bananas.

Vacuuming and carpet cleaning are two different things. You're not eating off of the floor. I'd venture that the bulk of Americans have never used a carpet cleaner in their homes and those who own and use them don't use them even this often... It's just fine. Your feet aren't going to fall off because they're only carpet cleaning once a month. ;)

I understand the difference between the two and have used a carpet cleaner many times. You can rent them from almost every local supermarket so they are not as rare as you would think.

I also understand the idea behind destroying the carpets by doing it too much and it makes sense from a certain perspective.

However I highly doubt that store managers are having their carpets cleaned just for the heck of it and there is obviously some need for more frequent cleanings. Given the high traffic of a restaurant I don't blame them either.

But it just sounds bad when the head of the company is telling his stores to "clean less" because it's too expensive.

I didn't say they were rare. I said the bulk of the populace does not use them.

Most of the cleaning requirements are standards set forth by the corporation and enforced by the franchise owner. They cleaned their carpets that often because they chose to do so and pushed the directive down to the franchise-level owners (it's just the way franchises work).

It honestly isn't that mind boggling to me. In fact, I'd even suggest that the bulk of the restaurants you go to on a regular basis clean their carpets (with an actual carpet cleaner, not a vacuum) much less than that. It usually only gets done when it's absolutely necessary.

Carpet Cleaner here. Hot water extraction is just one way to professionally clean a carpet. Frequent vacuuming, encapsulation cleaning (like dry-cleaning a shirt), use of a spotter for spills, and quarterly or even semi annual hot water extraction should be more than sufficient for commercial restaurant carpet (CGD). Unless you work at "We Fry Everything".

Once a month for a carpet washing may be excessive (depending on the type of commercial carpet).

Vacuuming though, should be done nightly at every eatery after closing (along with sanitizing the washrooms).
